full_judgment:
Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury, J.- This appeal by the plaintiff Sreemati Tripti Lata Kar against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 411 of 1969 arising out 91 suit for declaration of the plaintiffs' right of permanent residence and that he is not liable to be evicted from the disputed premises or in the alternative for permanent injunction restraining the Defdt. Nos. 1 and 2 from any way interfering with the plaintiffs' long standing possession in the suit premises. 

 4. The defdt. No.2 contested the suit by filing written statement. The case of the defdt. No. 2 was that the suit premises belonged to Babu Nikhil Chandra Kar and was duly recorded in his name during the last settlement operation. That the suit land has been declared enemy property as the owner is an Indian National. The plaintiff lives with her husband in the tea garden who is garden employee. The plaintiff with a view to grab the suit land has created the so called memorandums in collusion with her husband and brother. The plaintiff did not reside in the suit premises as claimed in the plaint. Therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed. The Trial Court decreed the suit on contest with cost with the finding that the marriage in domesticated form which provides daughter with residence in the paternal home and for her maintenance as members of the father's family is recognised by Dayabhaga School of Hindu Law. The plff. was given in marriage in the suit premises in domesticated form and she has been residing in the suit premises since her birth as a member of her father's family. Such right of plaintiff was recognised by her brother who inherited the suit premises from his father by Ext.1. That her possession is quite lawful and she is therefore, not liable to be evicted as a trespasser. 

 In the result, we allow the appeal with cost and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the Court of appeal below.
